einzeiler: Comedian Mike Glazer discusses his battle with OCD, bipolar symptoms, and cannabis.
kurzfassung: Comedian Mike Glazer joins the show to discuss his experiences with roller hockey, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and navigating mental health struggles. The conversation explores the intersection of comedy, cannabis use, and psychiatric diagnoses like bipolar disorder. They also examine the importance of therapy, community support programs, and the challenges of modern discourse.
stichpunkte: Mike Glazer shares his background as a top roller hockey goalie and how sports served as a safe haven for his childhood anxiety and OCD.
The discussion covers familial mental health history, including schizophrenia, depression, and bipolar disorder.
The hosts analyze how high-potency cannabis can trigger anxiety, panic, and manic episodes in certain individuals.
Glazer reflects on the profound impact of losing his therapist and the subsequent two-year period of instability.
The psychological risks and potential therapeutic uses of psychedelics like ketamine, LSD, and psilocybin are evaluated.
Al-Anon and 12-step programs are highlighted as powerful tools for addressing codependency, personal accountability, and regret.
The parallels between athletic superstitions, pigeon behaviorism experiments, and human rituals are explored.
Dave Chappelle's comedy career, the responsibilities of celebrity, and the complexities of public discourse are debated.

Comedy, Dave Chappelle, and Cultural Discourse

clips.hook: Why a childhood lack of size led to playing roller hockey goalie
clips.text: Growing up as an overweight child during the popularity of the Mighty Ducks, the speaker gladly accepted the position of target practice because it offered a way to belong.

clips.hook: The inevitable anxiety trap of long-term cannabis use
clips.text: Research consistently shows that chronic marijuana consumption eventually triggers increased anxiety, while users mistakenly rely on more of the substance to treat the very problem it causes.

clips.hook: Quarterly mushroom trips and physical discomfort
clips.text: Taking a substantial dose of psilocybin every few months provides an internal reset after dealing with digestive discomfort and nausea.

clips.hook: An impulsive Vegas trip spent entirely watching Showtime
clips.text: An unannounced drive to a luxury hotel resulted in holing up inside a suite for two days straight to stream television shows while avoiding food, running up a bill of over one thousand dollars.

clips.hook: When do quirky habits officially cross the line into OCD?
clips.text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is officially diagnosed when repetitive actions are tied to intrusive thoughts and begin actively disrupting daily functioning.

beschreibung:
This week, Dr. Drew talks with comedian and writer Mike Glazer, whose journey has taken him from the roller hockey rink to the comedy stage. Mike shares insights into his experiences with mental health, including struggles with OCD, depression, and family challenges. He opens up about shifting from partying tales to more introspective stand-up, as well as the therapeutic benefits of Al-Anon and weekly therapy. Dr. Drew and Mike also discuss the nuances of cannabis use and explore comedy’s complex role in addressing societal issues.
